title: Company OKR Initiative Atlas: prioritization, owners, and release phases
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build an "Initiative Atlas" — a single, consumable artifact that maps company-level OKRs to prioritized initiatives, named owners, release phases, and visible dependencies across Eng, Design, and Ops. The Atlas will be used by execs, product leads, and GTM to make release trade-offs, commit capacity to Dedicated and Private product workstreams, and validate that SLAs and compliance initiatives are scheduled appropriately.

Goal: Produce a prioritized, phase-aware map that: (1) surfaces unresolved dependencies and blockers; (2) shows owners and tentative milestone dates; (3) ties initiatives to measurable OKR outcomes and leading indicators; (4) provides a living cadence for weekly updates and rollback decisions.

Why now: Multiple Q1 initiatives have overlapping infra and runtime dependencies (model serving kernel upgrades, Dedicated capacity autoscaling features, and Console rollout steps). Without a consolidated view, we risk misaligned releases, double-booked capacity, and unclear accountability for quality regressions.

Deliverables:
- Initiative Atlas (Google Sheet + interactive Confluence page) that includes initiative name, primary owner, contributing teams, OKR mapping, phase (Plan / Build / Canary / GA), tentative release window, risks, blockers, and key metrics.
- Dependency lattice visualization exported as PNG/SVG for exec decks.
- Weekly cadence doc and update template for owners to publish progress and blockers.
- Rollout decision rubric for canary vs immediate GA when regressions occur.

Success metrics:
- All company-level initiatives (>=95%) mapped to an Atlas entry by 2026-03-12.
- Reduction in execution conflicts: fewer than 2 cross-team resource conflicts/week reported to PM leadership during March.
- 2 release decisions during Q1 that reference the decision rubric in postmortems.

Stakeholders:
- Executive sponsor: Priya Menon (COO)
- PM leads: Owen Ramirez (Platform PM), Aisha Kapoor (owner)
- Eng leads: Maya Alvarez (Serving Runtime), Ben O'Neill (Console)
- Design lead: Noor Patel
- GTM/contact: Sara Lindstrom (Growth)

Proposed approach and timeline:
1) 2026-02-21 to 2026-02-28: Intake sprint — PMs submit initiative summaries using canonical template (OKR tie, owner, phase, rough estimates, known deps).
2) 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-05: Cross-team workshop to reconcile dependencies and propose release phases. Include Simulation: model upgrade windows vs Dedicated capacity schedule.
3) 2026-03-06 to 2026-03-12: Synthesize Atlas and produce dependency lattice + initial exec briefing.
4) Ongoing weekly updates: owners update row status; PM owner (Liam) publishes rollup and highlights blockers to execs.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Granularity vs maintenance cost: Do we track per-subtask milestones (high fidelity) or only initiative-level phases (lower overhead)? Proposal: start initiative-level; escalate to milestone tracking for initiatives with cross-team critical-path impact.
- Release rigidity: Mixing GA dates for customer-facing features and infra-only rollouts may create false confidence. Proposal: separate "customer impact" flag and require a canary window for infra affecting runtime or KV cache behavior.

Links to artifacts:
- Intake template (Google Sheet): https://drive.google.com/example/initiative-atlas-intake
- Confluence Atlas draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Initiative+Atlas+Draft
- Dependency lattice sketch (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/example/dependency-lattice

Next steps (this ticket):
- Send intake template to PM leads by 2026-02-21 (Aisha) — DONE 2026-02-21
- Schedule cross-team workshop and invite Eng/Design leads — IN PROGRESS (invites sent 2026-02-25)
- Curate initial Atlas rows for 12 priority initiatives and share with execs by 2026-03-06 (owner: Liam)

Risks and mitigation:
- Missing inputs from initiative owners — mitigation: PM sends reminders and flags in weekly GTM sync; escalate after 48h.
- Unresolved infra capacity conflicts — mitigation: temporary blocking policy and tagging of impacted initiatives for priority triage meeting.

Longer-term plan: If the Initiative Atlas proves effective, embed into Redwood Console as a cross-team rollout dashboard (release: console-2026.2) with API hooks to pull runtime SLAs and capacity forecasts for Dedicated customers.
